units: pixels (full-resolution 3840x2160 image coordinates, x right, y down) and seconds; no metric scale

camera.evidence: phase correlation of a static seabed patch (x 500-1250, y 1240-1600) vs frame 0: |shift| <= 0.03 px for all frames (scripts/camcheck.py)
camera.view: side view, horizontal line of sight; whale swims in a plane roughly parallel to the image (2D scene). Seabed recedes in perspective below y ~1260, but the whale and its motion are treated as one plane.

objects.name: whale
objects.description: single large blue humpback-type whale (long pectoral flippers, small dorsal hump), the only moving object; swims right-to-left (head left), slight downward-then-upward tail stroke
objects.partially_out_of_frame: frames 0-46 the tail/fluke is cut by the right image edge (x = 3839); whole whale visible frames 47-71 (frame 47 fluke tip touches x 3831, so 48/49+ is safest)

reference_points.ref_x/ref_y: mask centroid (proxy for the rig origin / body centre); biased toward the head in frames 0-46 because the tail is cut off
reference_points.snout_x/snout_y: leftmost mask pixel (snout tip), integer, noise ~ +-5 px
reference_points.jaw_front_x: mean leftmost mask x over rows 880-979 (front of the lower head), smoothest translation reference, noise ~ +-2-3 px
reference_points.front_x_780_880: mean leftmost mask x over rows 780-879

full_length_bbox_w_uncut_frames_47_71.note: snout to fluke tip, horizontal; decreases late (frames 60-71) as the tail bends upward

bbox_height_uncut.note: vertical extent incl. flipper (and raised fluke late)

motion_summary_px.per_frame_step: jaw_front_x step ~ -12 px/frame early, ~ -12 to -15 px/frame late (see csv)
motion_summary_px.vertical: head nearly level (snout_y ~820-835, head_cy ~842-847); centroid ref_y 885 -> 943 (f27) -> 822 (f71) driven by tail bend + tail cut

objects.name: whale_shadow
objects.description: dark elongated shadow of the whale on the seabed (y ~1560-1700), moves with the whale
objects.note: cut by right edge frames 0-30; bbox from Lab-L < 105 threshold, can merge with the rock/coral at the left end

objects.name: rock
objects.description: pale speckled boulder on the seabed, lower left

objects.name: coral_bush
objects.description: dark branching coral/sea-fan just left of the rock

objects.name: seaweed_stalks
objects.description: 5 thin dark kelp stalks on the seabed, left of / behind the rock

objects.name: seabed
objects.description: sandy floor with moving caustic light patterns; far edge (floor/water boundary) at y ~1260

objects.name: water_surface_and_mid_water
objects.description: rippled water surface seen from below at the top (y < ~600), darker mid-water band y ~700-1260, faint pale vertical streaks at top-right (x 3550-3840, y ~690-760) are background texture

events.note: snout already moving at frame 0->1 (947->939) though jaw_front_x is flat 0->1 (1058.5->1058.6); treat motion as ongoing for the whole clip

events.event: tail tip leaves contact with right image edge (whole whale in frame)
tail lowest (max downward bend): bottom_y max 1648, centroid ref_y max 942.7
tail sweeps upward; fluke above the body top from ~frame 52 (bbox_y0 drops 593 -> 187 at f71)
no impacts, contacts, bounces or releases; no other moving objects
